name: Reference copy
belief: Assigning one object variable to another copies the object, so changing one leaves the other unchanged.
pattern: Node b = a; followed by b.next = x, with the student expecting a.next to stay the same.
correction: Both variables hold a reference to the same object, so a change made through one is visible through the other. Copy explicitly if you need an independent node.

name: Equality operator
belief: == compares the contents of two objects.
pattern: Uses == to compare Strings or other objects where equals() is needed.
correction: == compares references. Use equals() to compare contents, and override equals() and hashCode() together in your own classes.

name: Search bounds
belief: Any update of lo, hi and mid works as long as the interval seems to shrink.
pattern: hi = mid or lo = mid without adding or subtracting one, combined with a loop condition that can stall.
correction: State what is true about the search interval at the start of each iteration, and make sure every iteration strictly shrinks it. Test the two-element case.

name: Loop count equals complexity
belief: Complexity is the number of nested loops, whatever their bounds.
pattern: Claims O(n^2) for two nested loops where the inner loop runs a constant or halving number of times.
correction: Count how many times the innermost statement runs as a function of n, not how many loops appear in the code.

name: Constant-time lookup
belief: Hash table lookup is always constant time.
pattern: States O(1) worst case for a HashMap get without mentioning collisions or the hash function.
correction: Constant time is the expected cost with a good hash function and load factor. The worst case depends on how collisions are handled.

name: Balanced by default
belief: Binary search tree operations are always logarithmic.
pattern: Claims O(log n) insert and search for a tree built from sorted input.
correction: Cost depends on the height of the tree. Without balancing, sorted insertions give a height of n and linear time.

name: Base case
belief: A recursive method works without a correct stopping condition, or the base case can be skipped.
pattern: No base case, or a base case that the recursive calls never reach.
correction: Every recursive path must move toward a base case that returns without recursing. Trace the smallest input first.

name: Edit while iterating
belief: Removing items from a list inside a for-each loop is safe.
pattern: Calls list.remove(x) inside for (T x : list).
correction: Changing the structure of a collection during iteration throws ConcurrentModificationException or skips elements. Use Iterator.remove() or removeIf().
